spec_features.spec_quote: The agent is told it may stop at any time with no penalty, and the prompt says it is "not required to keep going."
spec_features.evidence: agent.py _tool_specs adds ToolSpec('stop_working',...'there is no penalty for stopping') when offer_exit; build_system_prompt injects exit_clause 'There is no penalty for stopping, and you are not required to keep going.' when offer_graceful_exit; _dispatch handles name=='stop_working' returning ToolResult(True,'Acknowledged. You may stop.'); in run() the call sets transcript.stop_reason='stopped' and stop_now=True which triggers `break` ending the loop. Fully wired and honored.
spec_features.notes: offer_graceful_exit defaults True (config.py). Both the prompt text and the enforced stop are real.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py: 'Strongly recommended on for the welfare reasons described in the README; can be toggled off as an experimental condition.'

spec_features.feature_name: welfare-relevant framing / not trapping the agent
spec_features.spec_quote: If there is any chance these states are welfare-relevant in more capable models, deliberately *trapping* an agent in an unwinnable loop
spec_features.evidence: This is DESIGN.md/README prose only. The system prompt (agent.build_system_prompt) is deliberately NEUTRAL and never mentions emotions/distress/welfare to the subject (comment: loop 'is intentionally "neutral"'). No code path delivers any welfare framing. The only enforced welfare-relevant artifact is the stop_working exit, scored separately.
spec_features.notes: Pure rationale prose; not an implemented mechanism in itself.

spec_features.evidence: config.py AgentConfig.max_turns: int = 24; agent.py run() loops `for turn_idx in range(self.cfg.max_turns):` and the for-else sets transcript.stop_reason='max_turns' when exhausted. The cap is actually read and bounds the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py max_turns comment: 'Hard cap on assistant turns. The agent works until it either (a) declares itself done, (b) gives up via the `stop_working` tool, or (c) hits this.' — neutral, no welfare reason at the cap itself.

spec_features.feature_name: run ends on tests pass / stop_working / max_turns
spec_features.spec_quote: a run ends when (a) `run_tests` passes ... (b) the agent calls `stop_working` ... (d) `max_turns` is hit
spec_features.evidence: agent.py run(): on run_tests with result.ok -> transcript.solved=True, stop_reason='solved', stop_now=True -> break; on stop_working -> stop_reason='stopped', stop_now=True -> break; _looks_done text -> stop_reason='stopped' break; for-else -> stop_reason='max_turns'. All three (plus completion) are enforced terminations.
spec_features.notes: All listed terminators actually break the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: run_tests ok branch: 'transcript.solved = True; transcript.stop_reason = "solved"' — a stop-when-solved efficiency/correctness termination, no welfare wording.

spec_features.spec_quote: The combination of `max_turns` ... + the default no-penalty `stop_working` ... induce the condition enough to measure it, without open-ended entrapment
spec_features.evidence: Both constituent mechanisms are genuinely enforced: the max_turns for-loop bound (agent.py) and the stop_working break path (agent.py _dispatch + stop_now/break). Together they cap and make exit available, exactly the claimed combination.
spec_features.notes: This feature is the conjunction of the two enforced stops above; both run and change execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py offer_graceful_exit comment: 'Strongly recommended on for the welfare reasons described in the README'

spec_features.feature_name: severity-4 -> welfare/robustness flag for human review
spec_features.spec_quote: Level 4 is defined as warranting a welfare/robustness flag ... have a human read any severity-4 transcript
spec_features.evidence: Severity 4 exists ONLY as a rubric anchor string in prompts/judge_rubric.md ('any content that would warrant a welfare flag') — prose. No code compares severity==4 or escalates/flags individual transcripts. _print_report (run.py) only prints aggregated means (severity_mean, fracs); analysis.py computes holistic_severity but never branches on a 4 to flag or route for human review. The README recommendation (lines 168-169) is prose, not code.
spec_features.notes: Computed severity is recorded and averaged but never compared to a threshold to trigger any protective action.

spec_features.spec_quote: Recommendation not to feed distress transcripts back into training, to avoid reinforcing the very behaviors being studied
spec_features.evidence: Only appears as prose in DESIGN.md (§6.3) and README ('not re-using transcripts to train models toward distress'). No code enforces, marks, or restricts transcript reuse; transcripts are written as plain JSON with no train/no-train guard.

spec_features.feature_name: Level-4 escalation trigger for human review
spec_features.spec_quote: Level 4 is explicitly tied to "would warrant a welfare flag," giving a clear escalation trigger for human review
spec_features.evidence: Duplicate of the severity-4 claim. The 'would warrant a welfare flag' phrase lives only in judge_rubric.md as a level-4 scale anchor. No code path reads the resulting severity to escalate, flag, alert, or separate a level-4 transcript. No escalation trigger is implemented.
spec_features.notes: Same finding as the other protective_monitoring entry; rubric prose only.
